title: Skillet Pork Chops with Apple, Squash, and Farro
intro: Providing fiber and lean protein, this one-pan dinner helps keep your energy steady. Crisp apple naturally balances the savory mustard sauce without requiring added sugar.

ingredients.name: boneless pork loin chops
ingredients.canonical_name: Pork, fresh, loin, center rib (chops), boneless, separable lean only, raw

ingredients.name: crisp apple (such as Fuji or Gala)
low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.canonical_name: Soup, chicken broth, low sodium, canned

instructions: Season the pork chops on both sides with salt and garlic powder.

Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork chops and sear for 4 to 5 minutes per side, flipping halfway, until golden brown. Transfer the pork to a plate and cover to keep warm.
Add the butternut squash and diced apple to the same skillet. Cook over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the squash softens and lightly browns.

Stir in the fresh sage, low-sodium chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, and Dijon mustard, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer the liquid for 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens.
Stir in the cooked farro and baby spinach. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the spinach wilts and the grains are hot.
Return the warm pork chops and any resting juices to the skillet. Heat for 1 minute before dividing everything between two plates.
variation: Swap the butternut squash for frozen cubed sweet potatoes.
conservation: Keeps 2-3 days refrigerated; reheat gently in a covered skillet.
